name: fdeflate (safe-Rust inflate, PNG-tuned)
baseline: flate2 1.1 with its default miniz_oxide backend, streaming inflate in 4096-byte chunks
verdict_reason: The decoder ran 1.5x to 1.6x faster than miniz_oxide and ahead of zlib-rs on Zen 4 and Apple M4, but only through a proof-of-concept flate2 adapter on a patched fork. The published 0.3.x crate has its own API and only an ultra-fast compression mode, so the general deflate numbers are not yet available to users.
tier_reason: Public harness branch (Shnatsel/flate2_bench, fdeflate branch) with rustc version, LLVM version and CPUs stated.
claimed_speedup: Inflate 815.348 vs 533.374 MB/s on Zen 4 (1.53x) and 677.090 vs 416.072 MB/s on Apple M4 (1.63x), also ahead of zlib-rs (721.516 and 527.478 MB/s); level-6 deflate 23.136 vs 13.772 MB/s on Zen 4 (1.68x) (ratios derived from page data).
workload: silesia-small.tar through flate2's streaming API in 4096-byte chunks, using a proof-of-concept fdeflate backend for flate2.
platforms: Any Rust target; checksums come from simd-adler32
one_liner: Safe-Rust deflate decoder from image-rs; inflated 1.5x to 1.6x faster than miniz_oxide in a flate2 prototype.
how_it_is_fast: Larger Huffman lookup tables (up to 4096 entries) sized for modern L1 caches, decoding two literals per table lookup, and cheaper table construction with fewer random writes. It does this without unsafe code in the crate itself.
use_it_when: You decode PNG or other zlib streams in memory and can call fdeflate's own API
You want a faster inflate without adding unsafe code or C to the dependency tree
skip_it_when: You need a flate2 backend today: the adapter in flate2 PR 545 is a closed proof of concept
You need general compression levels 1 to 9: the released 0.3.x encoder only has an ultra-fast PNG mode
You rely on preset dictionaries, which fdeflate lacks
caveats: Numbers come from an unmerged prototype that depends on a fork exposing private fdeflate state
Measured by a member of the image-rs organization, which maintains fdeflate
One input file; compression heuristics are tuned for PNG and gave slightly worse ratios on silesia
tradeoffs: Compression ratio at level 1 was 1.555 against 1.991 for miniz_oxide in the same run
No streaming flate2 integration yet; the prototype needed an extra copy for the lookback window
